source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Equivalent completeness criteria
statement: For R, the least-upper-bound property, monotone convergence, nested intervals, Bolzano-Weierstrass, and the Cauchy criterion are equivalent (with the Archimedean property where needed).
conditions: The ordered field is R or an Archimedean complete ordered field.
conclusion: Any one of these completeness principles can replace the others in proofs.
typical_uses: Select the most efficient completeness form for a convergence argument.
common_misuses: Using nested intervals alone in a non-Archimedean ordered field.
bridge_lemmas: Bounded monotone sequences converge; Cauchy sequences are bounded.
repair_templates: State the completeness principle and any Archimedean assumption explicitly.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Cauchy criterion
statement: A real sequence converges iff for every epsilon>0, all sufficiently late terms differ by less than epsilon.
conditions: The sequence is real-valued.
conclusion: Convergence can be proved without first identifying the limit.
typical_uses: Establish convergence of recursively defined or series partial-sum sequences.
common_misuses: Assuming the criterion holds in an incomplete space such as Q.
bridge_lemmas: A Cauchy sequence is bounded and has a convergent subsequence in R.
repair_templates: If working in Q, pass to R or prove the limit lies in Q.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Cauchy criterion for series
statement: The series sum a_n converges iff every sufficiently late finite tail sum a_{m+1}+...+a_n has arbitrarily small absolute value.
conditions: a_n is a real sequence.
conclusion: Series convergence is equivalent to the Cauchy property of partial sums.
typical_uses: Prove convergence and derive comparison tests.
common_misuses: Checking only that a_n tends to zero.
bridge_lemmas: Convergence of a series implies its terms tend to zero.
repair_templates: Control arbitrary tails rather than only single terms.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Alternating series test
statement: If a_n is nonnegative, decreasing, and tends to zero, then sum (-1)^(n+1)a_n converges.
conditions: a_n >= 0 and a_{n+1} <= a_n.
conclusion: The alternating series converges (generally conditionally).
typical_uses: Handle conditionally convergent series and error estimates.
common_misuses: Omitting monotonicity or nonnegativity.
bridge_lemmas: Even and odd partial sums are monotone and interlaced.
repair_templates: Verify eventual monotonicity and apply the test to the tail.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Absolute convergence and rearrangements
statement: An absolutely convergent series remains convergent with the same sum under every permutation of its terms.
conditions: sum |a_n| converges.
The rearrangement is a bijective permutation of N.
conclusion: Reordering does not change the sum.
typical_uses: Justify changing summation order or grouping terms.
common_misuses: Reordering a merely conditionally convergent series.
bridge_lemmas: Absolute convergence makes tails uniformly small under finite omissions.
repair_templates: Add absolute convergence or avoid rearrangement.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem
statement: Every bounded sequence in R has a convergent subsequence with limit in R.
conditions: The sequence is bounded in R.
conclusion: Boundedness yields sequential compactness of R intervals.
typical_uses: Extract convergent subsequences in compactness and Cauchy proofs.
common_misuses: Assuming the whole sequence converges or omitting boundedness.
bridge_lemmas: Nested interval construction or supremum arguments provide the subsequence.
repair_templates: State boundedness and use only a subsequence conclusion.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Sequential criterion for functional limits
statement: lim_{x->c} f(x)=L iff every sequence x_n in the domain with x_n != c and x_n->c satisfies f(x_n)->L.
conditions: c is a limit point of the domain.
conclusion: Sequential testing completely characterizes a real functional limit.
typical_uses: Disprove limits by constructing two approaches.
common_misuses: Allowing x_n=c or using sequences outside the domain.
bridge_lemmas: Negating epsilon-delta produces a counterexample sequence with delta=1/n.
repair_templates: Check domain membership and exclude the center point.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Sequential characterization of continuity
statement: f is continuous at c iff x_n->c in its domain always implies f(x_n)->f(c); at a limit point this is equivalent to lim_{x->c}f(x)=f(c).
conditions: c belongs to the domain of f.
conclusion: Continuity can be checked entirely by sequences.
typical_uses: Prove continuity of compositions and detect discontinuities.
common_misuses: Using a functional limit without requiring c in the domain.
bridge_lemmas: Algebraic combinations preserve continuity when defined.
repair_templates: Separate the point-value condition from the punctured limit.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Heine-Borel compactness
statement: For K subset R, the following are equivalent: K is closed and bounded; every sequence in K has a subsequence converging in K; every open cover has a finite subcover.
conditions: K is a subset of R.
conclusion: Closed bounded subsets of R are compact in sequential and open-cover senses.
typical_uses: Obtain extrema, uniform continuity, and convergent subsequences.
common_misuses: Applying compactness to an unclosed interval or an arbitrary metric space without proof.
bridge_lemmas: Bolzano-Weierstrass plus closedness gives sequential compactness.
repair_templates: Check both closedness and boundedness before invoking compactness.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Extreme value theorem
statement: A continuous real function on a nonempty compact set attains both its maximum and minimum.
conditions: f is continuous.
The domain is nonempty and compact.
conclusion: There exist points where f reaches global sup and inf.
typical_uses: Prove boundedness, optimization, and existence of extrema.
common_misuses: Using it on open or unbounded domains.
bridge_lemmas: Continuous images of compact sets are compact.
repair_templates: Restrict to a closed bounded interval or establish compactness separately.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Uniform continuity on compact sets
statement: Every continuous function on a compact subset of R is uniformly continuous.
conditions: f is continuous on compact K.
conclusion: A single delta works for every point of K for each epsilon.
typical_uses: Upgrade pointwise continuity to uniform estimates.
common_misuses: Assuming continuity on arbitrary noncompact sets gives uniform continuity.
bridge_lemmas: A failure of uniformity yields two sequences whose distance tends to zero.
repair_templates: Add compactness or prove a global Lipschitz bound.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Intermediate value theorem
statement: If f is continuous on [a,b], every value between f(a) and f(b) is attained at some c in [a,b].
conditions: f is continuous on a closed interval.
conclusion: The image of an interval is an interval.
typical_uses: Prove existence of roots and fixed points.
common_misuses: Using it for discontinuous functions or on disconnected domains.
bridge_lemmas: Closed intervals are connected; continuous images preserve connectedness.
repair_templates: Verify endpoint values and continuity on the entire interval.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Mean value theorem
statement: If f is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), some c in (a,b) satisfies f'(c)=(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a).
conditions: Continuity on the closed interval and differentiability on its interior.
conclusion: A secant slope equals an interior derivative.
typical_uses: Prove monotonicity, Lipschitz bounds, and uniqueness.
common_misuses: Ignoring endpoint continuity or interior differentiability.
bridge_lemmas: Rolle's theorem applied after subtracting the secant line.
repair_templates: Check the precise interval hypotheses before applying MVT.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Darboux theorem
statement: A derivative has the intermediate value property: if f'(a) and f'(b) straddle alpha, then f'(c)=alpha for some c between a and b.
conditions: f is differentiable on an interval containing [a,b].
conclusion: Derivatives need not be continuous but cannot have jump discontinuities.
typical_uses: Repair false claims that derivatives are continuous or monotone.
common_misuses: Assuming Darboux implies derivative continuity.
bridge_lemmas: Apply the interior-extremum theorem to f(x)-alpha x.
repair_templates: Replace continuity claims by the weaker intermediate value property.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Uniform limit theorem
statement: A uniform limit of continuous functions on a set is continuous; uniform convergence also permits termwise integration and, with uniform derivative convergence plus one-point convergence, termwise differentiation.
conditions: f_n are continuous and converge uniformly for continuity conclusion.
For differentiation, derivatives converge uniformly and f_n converge at one point.
conclusion: Uniform convergence transfers these operations to the limit.
typical_uses: Justify exchanging limits with continuity, integration, or differentiation.
common_misuses: Using pointwise convergence alone.
bridge_lemmas: Uniform Cauchy criterion controls tails independently of x.
repair_templates: Strengthen pointwise convergence to uniform or restrict to compact subdomains.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Weierstrass M-test
statement: If |f_n(x)|<=M_n for all x and sum M_n converges, then sum f_n converges uniformly and absolutely.
conditions: The majorant series sum M_n converges.
conclusion: The function series is uniformly convergent on its domain.
typical_uses: Establish uniform convergence of power and Fourier-type series.
common_misuses: Using bounds M_n that depend on x.
bridge_lemmas: Comparison test applied to tails gives uniform Cauchy control.
repair_templates: Find x-independent majorants, often on a compact interval.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Power-series interval of convergence
statement: If sum a_n x_0^n converges, then sum a_n x^n converges absolutely for every |x|<|x_0|; convergence therefore has a radius interval, with endpoint behavior separate.
conditions: A power series converges at x_0.
conclusion: Interior points converge absolutely; endpoints require individual tests.
typical_uses: Determine domains and justify compact uniform convergence.
common_misuses: Assuming endpoint convergence from interior convergence.
bridge_lemmas: Bound |a_n x_0^n| and compare with a geometric series.
repair_templates: Analyze each endpoint independently.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Lagrange remainder
statement: If f has N+1 derivatives near 0, then f(x)-sum_{n=0}^N f^(n)(0)x^n/n! equals f^(N+1)(c)x^(N+1)/(N+1)! for some c between 0 and x.
conditions: f is N+1 times differentiable on an interval containing 0 and x.
conclusion: Taylor error is bounded by a derivative bound times |x|^(N+1)/(N+1)! .
typical_uses: Prove Taylor convergence and quantitative approximation.
common_misuses: Assuming infinite differentiability alone makes the Taylor series equal f.
bridge_lemmas: Repeated generalized mean value theorem applied to the error.
repair_templates: Provide a uniform derivative bound before taking N to infinity.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Lebesgue criterion for Riemann integrability
statement: A bounded function on [a,b] is Riemann-integrable iff its discontinuity set has measure zero.
conditions: f is bounded on a compact interval.
conclusion: Integrability is characterized exactly by the size of the discontinuity set.
typical_uses: Show functions with countably many or Cantor-set discontinuities are integrable.
common_misuses: Applying the criterion without boundedness or confusing measure zero with countability.
bridge_lemmas: Sets of measure zero admit covers by intervals of arbitrarily small total length.
repair_templates: Establish boundedness and measure-zero discontinuities separately.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Fundamental theorem of calculus
statement: If f is integrable with antiderivative F, integral_a^b f=F(b)-F(a); conversely, the indefinite integral of integrable g is continuous and is differentiable at every continuity point of g with derivative g.
conditions: For part one f is integrable and F'=f; for part two g is integrable.
conclusion: Differentiation and integration are inverse under the stated regularity.
typical_uses: Evaluate integrals and identify derivatives of accumulated-area functions.
common_misuses: Claiming differentiability at discontinuities of g or assuming every derivative is Riemann-integrable.
bridge_lemmas: Mean value theorem controls increments on partitions.
repair_templates: State continuity at the point where the derivative conclusion is used.

source: Abbott, Understanding Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Differentiation under a proper integral
statement: If f(x,t) and its partial derivative f_x are continuous on a compact rectangle, then F(x)=integral_c^d f(x,t)dt is differentiable and F'(x)=integral_c^d f_x(x,t)dt.
conditions: Both f and f_x are continuous on the rectangle.
conclusion: Derivative and integral may be interchanged.
typical_uses: Justify parameter differentiation in analysis and special functions.
common_misuses: Interchanging operations without uniform domination or continuity.
bridge_lemmas: Compactness gives uniform continuity and boundedness.
repair_templates: Supply a uniform bound or compact-domain hypothesis.
